sections.title: Header — every setting
sections.summary: The top bar of the screen — the Back and Skip buttons and the progress indicator that shows how far along the visitor is. This guide documents every setting of the Header block, grouped by area. Each setting matches a real control in the screen editor.

sections.title: Header section
sections.summary: Controls the bar at the top of the screen: the Back and Skip buttons and the progress indicator that shows how far through the flow a visitor is. Most screens inherit sensible defaults — style the progress indicator (kind and colors) so it matches your brand.

sections.title: Where it appears
sections.summary: Covered screen types: HeroContent, Carousel, ListMultiPick, ListSinglePick, GridMultiPick, GridSinglePick, ProgressSteps, TextInput, WheelPicker, HeroList, WebEmbed.

sections.title: Header Bar Background
sections.summary: Fills the header bar with a color, or clear it to transparent so the screen background shows through for a floating header. Use a solid color to set the header apart from busy content. If you go transparent over a photo or video, check that the Back, Skip, and progress colors still stand out clearly.

sections.title: Header Bar Height
sections.summary: Sets how tall the header bar is, from 20 to 200 pixels, with a default of 44, which is the space its buttons and progress bar share. Keep it near the default for a standard bar and raise it only if you add a tall icon or larger text. Going too small cramps the Back and Skip buttons and makes them hard to tap.

sections.title: Header See-Through Level
sections.summary: Fades the whole header bar from fully solid to fully see-through, defaulting to solid. Lower it for a soft, partly transparent header that blends into a photo or video background. Keep it high enough that the Back, Skip, and progress controls stay easy to see.

sections.title: Back Button Label
sections.summary: Sets the text and styling of the Back control that returns visitors to the previous step. Defaults to a left arrow and supports other languages. Keep it small so it doesn't compete with your main action, and clear it to hide the button on the first screen, where there's nowhere to go back to.

sections.title: Back button text style
sections.summary: Overrides how the Back control's label looks — font, size, weight, color, alignment, line height, an optional highlight behind the text, and a strikethrough color. By default it inherits your project theme, which keeps every screen consistent. Touch this only when the Back label needs to match a specific header treatment, and keep it subtle so it never competes with your main action.

sections.title: Spacing inside the header
sections.summary: Sets the inner spacing on each side (top, right, bottom, left) that pushes the Back button, Skip button, and progress bar away from the header edges. Raise the top value to keep these controls clear of the phone's status bar or notch, and adjust left/right so buttons aren't jammed against the screen edge. Start from the defaults and nudge only where something looks cramped, since a clean header keeps the first impression of your ad landing page tidy.

sections.title: Completed Progress Color
sections.summary: Colors the filled, completed part of the progress bar. Defaults to gold for the Line style and teal for Dashes. Use your brand accent and make sure it clearly stands out against the unfilled track color so visitors can see at a glance how far they've come.

sections.title: Progress Content Side
sections.summary: Sets where the icon and label sit across the header, on the left (Start), centered, or on the right (End). Mostly a cosmetic touch: centered usually looks balanced, while left or right lets you line the label up with your Back or Skip button. Adjust only if the default looks off.

sections.title: Stretch Progress Edge-To-Edge
sections.summary: When on, the progress bar stretches all the way across the header; when off, it takes only the width its content needs. Use full width for a bold, obvious progress bar across the top of the screen. Turn it off when you want the bar compact and grouped with a label or icon.

sections.title: Header icon settings
sections.summary: Controls the optional header icon shown next to the progress bar — its image (upload or URL), placement relative to the label, scale mode, width, height, corner rounding, and padding. Off by default. Turn it on only to reinforce branding in the header, and keep the icon small so it doesn't crowd the progress bar or the Back and Skip buttons.

sections.title: Optional Header Icon
sections.summary: Adds an optional small icon, often a logo or step glyph, next to the progress bar, with controls for the image, its size, and its spacing. Most funnels leave this off. Use it only to reinforce branding in the header, and keep the icon small so it doesn't crowd the progress bar.

sections.title: Progress Bar Style
sections.summary: Chooses how progress through the funnel looks: a single continuous bar (Line) or segmented dots (Dashes), each with its own color controls below. A visible 'how far along' cue reassures visitors only a few steps remain, which lifts completion. Pick whichever fits your brand and keep it the same across screens.

sections.title: Spacing around the progress bar
sections.summary: Sets the spacing on each side of the progress indicator alone, separate from the header's overall padding. Use it to fine-tune the gap around the bar, for example to nudge it down from the buttons, without moving the buttons themselves. Most funnels keep the default; adjust only when the bar sits too tight or too loose against the header.

sections.title: Keep Progress Clear Of Buttons
sections.summary: When on, which is the default, the progress bar shrinks so it never overlaps the Back or Skip buttons; when off, it can collide with them in a tight header. Leave it on. Turn it off only if you've removed those buttons and want the bar to use the full width.

sections.title: Progress text style
sections.summary: Overrides how the progress label (for example 'Step 5 of 10') looks — font, size, weight, color, alignment, line height, an optional highlight, and a strikethrough color. By default it inherits your theme. Use it to make the reassurance text legible against your header background, and keep it small so it supports rather than overshadows the progress bar.

sections.title: Progress Bar Text
sections.summary: Optional text shown with the progress bar, such as a 'Step 5 of 10' counter or a short line of reassurance. Supports other languages and styling; leave it empty for a clean bar-only look. Note this text is fixed per screen and won't count up on its own, so use it as a label unless you drive it from a variable.

sections.title: Remaining Progress Color
sections.summary: Colors the empty, not-yet-completed part of the progress bar. Defaults to white for the Line style and light gray for Dashes. Keep it muted next to the filled color so the completed portion clearly reads as progress rather than blending in.

sections.title: Progress Height In Header
sections.summary: Sets where the progress bar sits up and down within the header: at the top, centered, or at the bottom. Centered is the usual balanced choice; use bottom to sit it just above your content, or top to hug the status bar. Adjust only if the default placement looks off for your header height.

sections.title: Skip Button Label
sections.summary: Sets the text and styling of the Skip control that lets visitors bypass this step. Defaults to 'SKIP' and supports other languages. Use it only where skipping is fine, and clear it to hide it on your paywall and key question screens, where an easy out lowers both sales and the answers you collect.

sections.title: Skip button text style
sections.summary: Overrides how the Skip control's label looks — font, size, weight, color, alignment, line height, an optional highlight, and a strikethrough color. By default it inherits your theme. Keep Skip visually quiet (smaller, lower-contrast) so it doesn't pull attention away from continuing; restyle it only to fit a specific header look.

sections.title: • Background opacity
sections.summary: How see-through the text background fill is, from 0% (invisible) to 100% (solid). Only matters when a background color is set.

sections.title: • Background radius
sections.summary: Corner rounding (px) of the text background fill; higher is softer.

sections.title: • Font family
sections.summary: The typeface of the back button.

sections.title: • Font size
sections.summary: Text size of the back button in pixels.

sections.title: • Font weight
sections.summary: How bold the text is, from Thin through Bold to Black.

sections.title: • Line height
sections.summary: Vertical spacing between lines of text — raise it to give multi-line text more breathing room.

sections.title: • Strikethrough color
sections.summary: Color of a line-through decoration when the text is struck out (for example, an old price).

sections.title: • Text align
sections.summary: Horizontal alignment of the text: start (left), center, or end (right).

sections.title: • Text background color
sections.summary: An optional fill drawn behind the back button text (a highlight pill). Off unless you set it; leave empty for plain text on the screen background.

sections.title: • Text color
sections.summary: The color of the back button text. Keep enough contrast with the background that it stays readable.

sections.title: • Corner radius
sections.summary: Rounding of the icon’s corners in pixels; raise it to clip a square image into a rounded or circular badge.

sections.title: • Enable icon
sections.summary: Off by default. Turn on to show a small image (for example a logo) in the header next to the progress indicator; off for no image.

sections.title: • Height
sections.summary: The icon’s height in pixels (0–200).

sections.title: • Icon image
sections.summary: Upload an image file or paste an image URL — the icon shown in the header. Leave empty to show no graphic.

sections.title: • Icon padding
sections.summary: The space around the icon (top, right, bottom, left) — the gap between the icon and the surrounding header content.

sections.title: • Placement
sections.summary: Where the icon sits relative to the progress title: Start (before it) or End (after it); the Fixed Start/End variants pin it to the header’s left/right edge; Top and Bottom stack it above or below.

sections.title: • Scale mode
sections.summary: How the image fits its box: Scale to Fill (stretch), Aspect Fit (show the whole icon, may letterbox), Aspect Fill (cover the box, may crop), or Center (no resize).

sections.title: • Width
sections.summary: The icon’s width in pixels (0–200).

subarticles.summary: Fades the whole header bar from fully solid to fully see-through, defaulting to solid. Lower it for a soft, partly transparent header that blends into a photo or video background. Keep it high enough that the Back, Skip, and progress controls stay easy to see.

subarticles.title: Header See-Through Level
subarticles.summary: Header See-Through Level

subarticles.title: Back Button Label
subarticles.summary: Sets the text and styling of the Back control that returns visitors to the previous step. Defaults to a left arrow and supports other languages. Keep it small so it doesn't compete with your main action, and clear it to hide the button on the first screen, where there's nowhere to go back to.

subarticles.title: Back button text style
subarticles.summary: Overrides how the Back control's label looks — font, size, weight, color, alignment, line height, an optional highlight behind the text, and a strikethrough color. By default it inherits your project theme, which keeps every screen consistent. Touch this only when the Back label needs to match a specific header treatment, and keep it subtle so it never competes with your main action.

subarticles.title: Back button text style
subarticles.summary: Back button text style

subarticles.title: • Background opacity
subarticles.summary: How see-through the text background fill is, from 0% (invisible) to 100% (solid). Only matters when a background color is set.

subarticles.title: • Background radius
subarticles.summary: Corner rounding (px) of the text background fill; higher is softer.

subarticles.title: • Font family
subarticles.summary: The typeface of the back button.

subarticles.title: • Font size
subarticles.summary: Text size of the back button in pixels.

subarticles.title: • Font weight
subarticles.summary: How bold the text is, from Thin through Bold to Black.

subarticles.title: • Line height
subarticles.summary: Vertical spacing between lines of text — raise it to give multi-line text more breathing room.

subarticles.title: • Strikethrough color
subarticles.summary: Color of a line-through decoration when the text is struck out (for example, an old price).

subarticles.title: • Text align
subarticles.summary: Horizontal alignment of the text: start (left), center, or end (right).

subarticles.title: • Text background color
subarticles.summary: An optional fill drawn behind the back button text (a highlight pill). Off unless you set it; leave empty for plain text on the screen background.

subarticles.title: • Text color
subarticles.summary: The color of the back button text. Keep enough contrast with the background that it stays readable.

subarticles.title: Spacing inside the header
subarticles.summary: Sets the inner spacing on each side (top, right, bottom, left) that pushes the Back button, Skip button, and progress bar away from the header edges. Raise the top value to keep these controls clear of the phone's status bar or notch, and adjust left/right so buttons aren't jammed against the screen edge. Start from the defaults and nudge only where something looks cramped, since a clean header keeps the first impression of your ad landing page tidy.

subarticles.title: Spacing inside the header
subarticles.summary: Spacing inside the header

subarticles.title: Completed Progress Color
subarticles.summary: Colors the filled, completed part of the progress bar. Defaults to gold for the Line style and teal for Dashes. Use your brand accent and make sure it clearly stands out against the unfilled track color so visitors can see at a glance how far they've come.

subarticles.title: Completed Progress Color
subarticles.summary: Completed Progress Color

subarticles.title: Progress Content Side
subarticles.summary: Sets where the icon and label sit across the header, on the left (Start), centered, or on the right (End). Mostly a cosmetic touch: centered usually looks balanced, while left or right lets you line the label up with your Back or Skip button. Adjust only if the default looks off.

subarticles.title: Progress Content Side
subarticles.summary: Progress Content Side

subarticles.title: Optional Header Icon
subarticles.summary: Adds an optional small icon, often a logo or step glyph, next to the progress bar, with controls for the image, its size, and its spacing. Most funnels leave this off. Use it only to reinforce branding in the header, and keep the icon small so it doesn't crowd the progress bar.

subarticles.title: Optional Header Icon
subarticles.summary: Optional Header Icon

subarticles.title: Header icon settings
subarticles.summary: Controls the optional header icon shown next to the progress bar — its image (upload or URL), placement relative to the label, scale mode, width, height, corner rounding, and padding. Off by default. Turn it on only to reinforce branding in the header, and keep the icon small so it doesn't crowd the progress bar or the Back and Skip buttons.

subarticles.title: Header icon settings
subarticles.summary: Header icon settings

subarticles.title: • Corner radius
subarticles.summary: Rounding of the icon’s corners in pixels; raise it to clip a square image into a rounded or circular badge.

subarticles.title: • Enable icon
subarticles.summary: Off by default. Turn on to show a small image (for example a logo) in the header next to the progress indicator; off for no image.

subarticles.title: • Height
subarticles.summary: The icon’s height in pixels (0–200).

subarticles.title: • Icon image
subarticles.summary: Upload an image file or paste an image URL — the icon shown in the header. Leave empty to show no graphic.

subarticles.title: • Icon padding
subarticles.summary: The space around the icon (top, right, bottom, left) — the gap between the icon and the surrounding header content.

subarticles.title: • Placement
subarticles.summary: Where the icon sits relative to the progress title: Start (before it) or End (after it); the Fixed Start/End variants pin it to the header’s left/right edge; Top and Bottom stack it above or below.

subarticles.title: • Scale mode
subarticles.summary: How the image fits its box: Scale to Fill (stretch), Aspect Fit (show the whole icon, may letterbox), Aspect Fill (cover the box, may crop), or Center (no resize).

subarticles.title: • Width
subarticles.summary: The icon’s width in pixels (0–200).

subarticles.title: Progress Bar Style
subarticles.summary: Chooses how progress through the funnel looks: a single continuous bar (Line) or segmented dots (Dashes), each with its own color controls below. A visible 'how far along' cue reassures visitors only a few steps remain, which lifts completion. Pick whichever fits your brand and keep it the same across screens.

subarticles.title: Progress Bar Style
subarticles.summary: Progress Bar Style

subarticles.title: Keep Progress Clear Of Buttons
subarticles.summary: When on, which is the default, the progress bar shrinks so it never overlaps the Back or Skip buttons; when off, it can collide with them in a tight header. Leave it on. Turn it off only if you've removed those buttons and want the bar to use the full width.

subarticles.title: Keep Progress Clear Of Buttons
subarticles.summary: Keep Progress Clear Of Buttons

subarticles.title: Progress Bar Text
subarticles.summary: Optional text shown with the progress bar, such as a 'Step 5 of 10' counter or a short line of reassurance. Supports other languages and styling; leave it empty for a clean bar-only look. Note this text is fixed per screen and won't count up on its own, so use it as a label unless you drive it from a variable.
